text:
The output stage is the most likely location of the fault. `vout_max` is about 1.7e-7 V, so the output is stuck low even though `vout` should swing to VDD. The largest sensitivity is M8 (-17.3% for +20%), meaning the output pull-down is overpowering the pull-up. M8 is the NMOS pull-down on `vout` (W=2.02 µm), about 5× the width of the other NMOS devices. The next most sensitive element is M7, the PMOS pull-up, and M4 is third, since it is the front-end PMOS that sets the upper trip point and its width is the next-most-sensitive. The likely fault is M8 being oversized, which makes the pull-down dominate the PMOS pull-up. This is an inference from the sensitivity data, since there is no operating-point data to confirm it.

```json
{"ranking": ["M8", "M7", "M4"], "fault": "M8 (output NMOS pull-down, gate x) is oversized at W=2.02 um relative to the pull-up M7 (4.039 um). Its strength overpowers the PMOS pull-up, so vout_max collapses to ~0 V and the high-level spec fails. Likely fix: reduce M8 width (e.g. back toward ~0.42-1 um) and re-check the M7/M8 ratio."}
```
